RESOLVED IN SUBSTANCE, correctly left open. The certification receipt now states this limitation itself rather than papering over it.

certification-report.md, verified by reading:

  line 42  "The artifact was built from the current workspace, not a named Git commit."
  line 43  "Current HEAD is b5d9a335..., which predates this work."
  line 45-46 "validation is not yet commit-reproducible. No release or durable certification
             claim should be made until the user authorizes and creates a commit containing
             this work."
  line 265 the Epic 0A deletions "were never committed and are not recoverable from Git.
           This receipt reconstructs the [record]"
  line 268 "the reason this report refuses to call the current workspace a release commit"

That is the right resolution and a better one than closing the bead would have been. The previous receipt asserted a SHA-256 over an uncommitted tree without saying so; this one names the hash, names HEAD, states that HEAD predates the work, and declines to call it a release. It also absorbs bd-01KZXJMDRC6VKYX6SA38R0AAH1 by recording that the deleted surface is unrecoverable rather than pretending a receipt exists for it.

The bead stays open because the underlying exposure is unchanged: 20 untracked R files and 40 modified tracked files, HEAD still b5d9a335. What changed is that the claim no longer overstates the evidence.

VERIFIED THIS PASS against the receipt:
  "49 test files and 362 tests"   actual 49 files, 362 test_that blocks - exact
  suite                            1822 pass, 0 fail, 0 error, 0 warn, 2 skip, 362 files

The two skips remain the scale gates from bd-01KZXEFHAWJ97VCRJ84JP85GA8, which the receipt also declares under explicitly unrun evidence.

Remaining action is one commit, and it belongs to the repository owner rather than to either agent.
